analysis: What changed vs Friday's 9:00 AM brief: the Friday selloff closed with the tape split — S&P 500 -0.40% to 7,561.67 and Nasdaq -0.91%, but the Dow +0.10%, and all three still ended the week higher (S&P +2.51%). The weekend's two big threads both center on Nvidia: the FT reports Jensen Huang is weighing a comeback with allies running a 'war room' to lobby the board and the White House, while Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly urged an outside CEO — so the governance story is now a tug-of-war into Tuesday's earnings, and Asia's chip rout (Taiwan -6.03%, TSMC -3.4%, SK Hynix -5.5%) shows the overhang is still spreading, not contained. The counterweight is Anthropic: ~7x oversubscribed per Bloomberg, pricing Wednesday and trading Thursday as ANT, which makes this week a live test of whether AI demand survives the Nvidia turmoil — note the circularity, with Nvidia putting up to $10B into the private placement while Anthropic owes ~$895B in compute commitments, mostly to Nvidia GPUs. Rates remain the other weight: the 10-year held 5.15% with a December hike now treated as all but certain, and Warsh speaks at noon ET today. Microsoft's outage fully resolving (root cause: a network capacity upgrade bug, no cyberattack) plus a Stifel upgrade removes one overhang and has MSFT +0.88% premarket. Bitcoin's weekend washout to ~$62,000 — a four-month low — before recovering to ~$64,600 is the risk-off tell in crypto. Signal vs noise: the Asia chip slide, the futures fade from Sunday evening's gains, and the 10-year above 5% are real; the Huang comeback talk is unconfirmed lobbying, not a decision, and Anthropic's oversubscription is a demand read, not a price — the verdict comes Wednesday/Thursday.
breadth_notes: Prior session (Fri Nov 13): more than 60% of S&P 500 stocks rose even as the index fell 0.40% (AP) — a rotational, tech-led decline, not a broad washout; the Dow gained 0.10% while the Nasdaq fell 0.91%. No fresh S&P 500 advance/decline ratio or volume-vs-20-day-average figures were shown by sourced pages.

community_signals.takeaway: Commenters are skeptical of Anthropic's moat: frontier models are seen as holding less than a year lead over China's best, and the durable edge is argued to be procurement contracts with Nvidia/Google and HBM supply, not the models themselves — a cooler read on the IPO than the 7x oversubscription headline alone.

headlines.headline: Futures point lower into Monday: at 5:08 AM ET, S&P 500 E-minis -0.36%, Nasdaq 100 E-minis -0.97%, Dow E-minis +0.02% (Reuters). Friday closed split: S&P 500 7,561.67 (-0.40%), Nasdaq 25,136.27 (-0.91%), Dow 52,347.55 (+0.10%) — all three still up for the week (S&P +2.51%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Futures reversed Sunday evening's small gains overnight — the tape opens on the back foot with the Nasdaq leading down, so the chip/AI complex sets the tone again.

headlines.headline: Jensen Huang is weighing a comeback as Nvidia CEO, the FT reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter: he has discussed returning with confidants, and an ally is assembling a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives to lobby the board and seek White House support. Nvidia and Huang declined to comment. Meanwhile Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday publicly urged an outside CEO. NVDA is down 1.6-2.2% premarket after falling ~13% last week to $162.85; earnings are Tue Nov 17, interim CEO Colette Kress's first call (consensus ~$111.2B revenue, ~$2.52 EPS).
headlines.why_it_matters: Comeback talk is unconfirmed lobbying, not a decision — the board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas and its Wachtell Lipton inquiry is still open — so the governance overhang stays live into earnings, and the stock keeps sliding premarket.

headlines.headline: Asia's chip rout deepened overnight: Taiwan's Taiex fell 6.03% (its second-largest point drop on record), Japan's Nikkei lost 2.42%, South Korea's Kospi fell 2.8%, with TSMC -3.4%, SK Hynix -5.5% and Samsung -3.2%. Japan's GDP shrank and China data missed, adding to the drag.
headlines.why_it_matters: The chip selloff is global and broadening beyond NVDA — Asian suppliers are pricing the same AI-valuation and Nvidia-leadership doubts before Tuesday's earnings.

headlines.headline: Anthropic's IPO is drawing orders for close to 7x the shares on offer, Bloomberg reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter — hotter demand than SpaceX at the same stage. Pricing is due Wed Nov 18, shares trade Thu Nov 19 on Nasdaq as ANT at $70-78; the company and backers seek up to $90.4B including a $26B private placement (Nvidia up to $10B, Google $10B, plus AMD, Microsoft, Micron, Broadcom, TSMC). Target valuation ~$1.4T. Anthropic disclosed ~$895.4B in compute commitments and $81B run-rate revenue as of Oct 31.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source (Bloomberg, unnamed people) but widely carried — the demand read is the week's counterweight to the Nvidia turmoil, and the debut becomes the live test of AI appetite; the $895B compute bill is the number to watch against that enthusiasm.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's 365 outage is fully resolved: 'all products are operational' and the email backlog has been processed, per Microsoft's service health update (Bloomberg). Root cause was a bug exposed during a network capacity upgrade that made Exchange servers consume all available resources; no cyberattack and unrelated to AI/agents. Microsoft apologized and will publish a preliminary report within two working days. MSFT is +0.88% premarket ($528.48), also helped by a Stifel upgrade calling the software giant 'getting back on track.'
headlines.why_it_matters: A three-day outage ending with a clear root cause and no security angle removes an enterprise-reliability overhang — and the Stifel upgrade gives the stock a second tailwind into the open.

headlines.headline: Fed focus today: Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at noon ET in San Francisco (AI and productivity), and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack also speaks Monday; FOMC minutes land Wednesday. Fed funds futures treat a December quarter-point hike as all but certain (odds of a half-point move fell to 6% from 12%). The 2-year yield fell more than 2 bps Monday after its biggest weekly jump in over two years on Friday. Empire State manufacturing prints at 8:30 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: With the hike fully priced, Warsh's tone is the day's rate signal — any hawkish surprise extends the pressure on growth multiples; a dovish lean would be the tape's easiest relief.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split premarket (Finnhub, 6:54 AM ET): AAPL +0.66% to $358.62 after a new 52-week high of $360.83 Friday and a +0.39% Friday close; MSFT +0.88%; META -0.59% to $637.88 after Friday's +2.90% close at $641.69; AMZN -0.05% to $266.52. Baidu's US shares are down more than 1% premarket after Q3 revenue of 30.81B yuan ($4.62B) came in essentially in line with the 30.86B yuan consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple and Microsoft are holding Friday's strength while Meta gives back some of its gain — the rotation within megacaps is narrowing to the names without fresh overhangs.
